On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Sources indicate that newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Recent findings suggest that brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

Recent findings suggest that we’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Sources indicate that will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

It has been revealed that borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

In a recent development, it is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Industry observers note that another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

According to recent reports, as reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Recent findings suggest that burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A significant year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

According to recent reports, enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

Industry observers note that A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

It has been revealed that newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

In a recent development, barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

#95944. England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence.
  • He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’.

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

It has been revealed that sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller.

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback.

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead.

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Industry observers note that spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

In a recent development, england had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

According to recent reports, england ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

Industry observers note that spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

Spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

In a recent development, pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

Industry observers note that england got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move.

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot.

The referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

There were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Industry observers note that eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Sources indicate that kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded.

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net.

It has been revealed that but then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

According to recent reports, the atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Recent findings suggest that now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

Le parcage d'Auguste-Delaune, de nouveau ouvert, et le Stade de Reims, étaient de nouveau prêts à les faire venir. Et ce, quelques heures avant le coup d'envoi du match. Sauf que la préfecture de la Marne, que nous avons contactée, ne l'a pas entendu de cette oreille et maintient : tout transport véhiculant des Stéphanois entrant dans le département sera intercepté et le parcage visiteur reste fermé.

Mais l'information n'a pas le temps de circuler. Le Stade de Reims l'apprend au dernier moment, pareil pour les supporters stéphanois déjà partis en bus. Certains rebroussent chemin, d'autres persistent. Ce qui donne une scène assez folle au péage de Champfleury, au sud de la Cité des Sacres. Les bus et minibus sont arrêtés par les forces de l'ordre et sommés de retourner d'où ils viennent. Près de 6 heures pour l'aller et la même chose pour le retour. Pour ces supporters, la rencontre se regardera sur la route... Cruel.

Ce qui n'est pas le cas d'autres, plus malins, qui avaient pris leur ticket dans d'autres tribunes, notamment tout proche du parcage resté vide. Munis d'ailleurs sous leur blouson de maillot et d'écharpe aux couleurs de l'ASSE, jusque-là bien cachés, mais qui ont été ressortis au coup d'envoi. Ceux-là, plusieurs centaines, ont pu donner de la voix, surtout après la victoire de leur club. Mais l'ambiance aurait pu prendre plus d'ampleur avec la présence de leurs partenaires. C'est quand même mieux un stade garni...".

La Préfecture de la Marne a manifestement oublié les grands principes de la Répubique : liberté, égalité, fraternité.

La conferenza stampa di Gennaro Gattuso in occasione della sfida casalinga contro il Lecce.

La sosta per gli impegni delle nazionali è finalmente giunta al termine, e le squadre di Serie A sono pronte a scendere in campo per la dodicesima giornata. In occasione del prossimo turno, la Lazio ospiterà allo stadio Olimpico di Roma il Lecce di Di Francese per la sfida in programma sabato 21 novembre alle ore 15:00. Dalla sala stampa del Training Center di Formello, il mister Gattuso è intervenuto in conferenza stampa per presentare il match contro i salentini.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that su Frattesi non devo riflettere, ha fatto tutto col gruppo, sta bene e a livello strumentale non ha nulla. Se oggi arriva e ha il raffreddore vediamo, ma ha fatto tutto. Isaksen e Provstgaard hanno fatto un lavoro in palestra come Dele-Bashiru e Belahyane. Tutti i giocatori hanno lavorato con noi. Zaccagni sta lavorando sul campo, c’è ancora un po’ di edema, ma riesce a gestire. Nuno ha cominciato riabilitazione in piscina con Sutalo. Marusic ha avuto una piccola ricaduta, sulla ricaduta che ha avuto un mese fa. Settimana prossima valutiamo in che condizione sono. Gli altri sono tutti a disposizione. Cataldi ieri non si è allenato, ha avuto un piccolo problema all’adduttore, ma pensiamo non sia nulla di grave.

Si pensa a domani, non a quello che dobbiamo fare dopo. Giochiamo contro una squadra solida e allenata bene, ha dieci punti in classifica. Ha vinto con l’Udinese e col Venezia, una squadra molto insidiosa sui calci piazzati. Dobbiamo prenderli con le pinze. Sta a noi come sempre. Servirà mentalità e voglia di stare in campo e giocare a ritmi elevati. È una partita molto difficile.

Ci può stare, ma per come giochiamo il modulo non c’entra niente. Dipende solo come andare a prendere gli avversari in pressing. L’importante è andare a occupare le posizioni libere, cambia poco. Conta la voglia, la partecipazione e la mentalità. Per questo, si può fare tutto, se andate a vedere quando facciamo pressioni stiamo solo con un vertice. Conta poco il modulo.

According to recent reports, non devo entrare solo nella sua, devo entrare nella testa di tutti. Lui è un giocatore importante ma ci sono anche gli altri. Bisogna capire cosa significa giocare poco. Sia Dele-Bashiru e Lazzari ci danno sempre un contributo quando entrano. Albert quando sta bene è un giocatore di altissimo livello. Domani tanti di loro che hanno trovato poco spazio avranno la possibilità di giocare dal primo minuto, ma sono tranquillo. L’importante è avere la consapevolezza che i giocatori hanno una buona condizione.

Per come sono fatto io non sono mai sereno, fa parte del mio modo di essere. Ho la consapevolezza che sono ragazzi che non si risparmiano mai. La qualità di corsa è alta, sono tutti ad un ottimo livello e questo mi riempie d’orgoglio. Domani dovremo far parlare in campo e metterlo in pratica.

Quando ho detto che non abbiamo niente da perdere mi hanno guardato storto, ma altri ragionamenti si fanno nelle ultime partite. Noi dobbiamo vivere partita dopo partita. Giochiamocela domani, poi vedremo dove si arriva. Io alleno una squadra che in questo momento deve vivere alla giornata. Le partite bisogna giocarle, importante è che non sbagliamo a livello di atteggiamento.

Industry observers note that ieri abbiamo visto la partita contro il Napoli, serve la mentalità, il guardarsi. Il veleno su ogni palla, quello deve essere nel nostro DNA. Siamo andati là e potevamo fare più di un gol, poi nel primo quarto d’ora potevamo perderla, poi siamo tornati in partita. Non bisogna dimenticare cosa ci ha portato qui. Se siamo qui è perchè giochiamo da squadra, perché non si molla di un centimetro. Poi si può sempre sbagliare, lo accettiamo sempre, l’importante è che non manchi la voglia di soffrire in campo. La squadra ha avuto miglioramenti, a volte siamo usciti dal campo e Mandas ci ha dato una mano, ma a livello di personalità abbiamo fatto un step importante. Bisogna lavorare sempre con personalità, senza dimenticare da dove siamo partiti.

Non mi piace fare il gitano, amo andare in giro e toccare con mano le mentalità di altri paesi. La mia crescita viene anche da tutti i giri che ho fatto. Noi italiani pensiamo sempre di essere i più forti, ma su tantissime cose nel calcio riesci a mettere dentro anche delle altre culture. Non penso se dovrò rimanere o meno, penso a quello che dovrò fare oggi. Sembra che io sia qui da dieci anni, mi sento a mio agio qui. Spero di rimanerci a lungo, difficilmente puoi trovare posti così.

Recent findings suggest that ho grande fiducia, vedo quello che fanno e come lavorano. Doekhi si è trovato fuori, ma quando ha giocato ha sempre fatto bene. C’è grande fiducia sul reparto difensivo. Pedraza non ha mai giocato, ma ha messo minutaggio da subentrato. C’è fiducia nei loro confronti. Romano? Ci sta che certe volte possa soffrire in fase difensiva, ma l’esperienza si fa giocando, con questo tipo di partite che sta giocando. Ci sta che possa subire questo tipo di partite. Siamo contenti che abbia rinnovato, ha grande voglia e senso di appartenenza.

Lui in questo momento per la mentalità che ha, può giocare anche a centrocampo e in difesa. Ha una convinzione e una condizione fisica incredibile. Lui può fare l’ala e l’ha dimostrato a Napoli, giocando con voglia e mentalità, ma può giocare ovunque. Non sono d’accordo con voi, avete massacrato Pinamonti dopo Napoli, si è speso tanto nel primo tempo. Nella ripresa abbiamo sofferto tutti, lui è in grandissima crescita.

Saranno affari loro se giocano alla playstation, non so nemmeno di che stai parlando. Non mi creo questo problema. Questo fa parte dell’essere professionista, di avere amor proprio del proprio lavoro. Non mi permetterei mai di chiedere ad un giocatore se ha dormito o meno. Vediamo domani mattina, ci sarà la colazione tutti insieme e mi metterò là concentrato e vedremo se qualcuno avrà fatto le ore piccole o meno.

It has been revealed that con lui abbiamo parlato, sapevo dove andare a parare. Si toccava con mano che tutto quello che era stato fatto non gli era entrato bene nella testa, ma ci sta: veniva da un calcio totalmente diverso. Tutte le nostre proposte erano arabo per lui, lo sapevo già. Da lì ha svoltato, gli ho detto che doveva chiedere ciò che non capiva e siamo rimasti di più in campo. Dopo gli è venuto più facile. Ci ha fatto vincere qualche partita, ma ci stava che all’inizio, avendo fatto cose totalmente diverse, avesse difficoltà. Sono sicuro che domani farà una grande partita.

According to recent reports, non è facile, anche un mese fa siamo stati fermi venti giorni. Non passano mai. Sappiamo quello che abbiamo dovuto fare, non è facile. Ci sono anche Champions, Europa e Conference. È una cosa di UEFA e FIFA che devono sedersi per mettersi d’accordo coi club, altrimenti non se ne esce fuori. Quando giocavo, a fine anno controllavo e avevo fatto 52 partite. Il problema è che adesso si gioca anche il venerdì e il sabato alle 15. I tempi di recupero sono diversi. Non siamo le persone adatte per lamentarci per quello che guadagnamo. I salari dei giocatori sono importanti, non vengo qua a lamentarmi.

Quella di domani. C’è poco da rispondere. I tre punti di domani sono uguali ai prossimi, non abbiamo priorità. L’avversario è diverso, ma per me è troppo difficile dirti cosa penso. Io penso alla gara di domani, poi vedremo cosa succederà a Torino. Come se adesso mi chiedessi del derby, so che tutti ci aspettano perché vogliono che vinciamo il derby, ma pensa come ci arrivo se ci comincio a pensare ora.

Ashley Cole accidentally shooting a student, bare-chested Marcus Bent threatening police with a meat cleaver - and an ex-Barcelona star firing a gun in a hospital! Footballers' fascination with weapons after Amar Dedic's bow and arrows saga

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE.
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE.

Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.

Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.

The Magpies star sparked a major police operation after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir outside Newcastle, with at least six patrol cars joining the search for the £30million player.

After tracking down and questioning the Bosnian, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public and that the equipment was intended for recreational use.

But Dedic's escapade was certainly not the first time a footballer has found himself in hot water over the possession, carrying or use of a weapon, with brass knuckles, meat cleavers and BB guns among the bizarre arsenal of items to have attracted the authorities' attention over the years.

Marcus Bent, with a meat cleaver, in Surrey.

Former Middlesbrough and Everton forward Marcus Bent was tasered in his own home by police after threatening armed police officers with a meat cleaver and kitchen knife while under the influence of cocaine.

Bent, who avoided jail in 2016 after he pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine and affray, called Surrey Police after thinking he had discovered an intruder in his home.

It has been revealed that officers arrived at the scene but were initially unable to gain access to the property. Guildford Crown Court heard how the officers were about to use a battering ram to gain entry when a bare-chested Bent 'flung' open the door holding two chef's knives, with his 'eyes wide, jaw clenched and his body rigid'.

Recent findings suggest that bent, who was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for two years, later remarked: 'I was paranoid and I was hallucinating. I felt there were people in my house. I remember thinking the door handle was moving.

Sources indicate that 'At no point was I ever going to take someone's life. I called them because I was hallucinating, paranoid, terrified.'.

Marcus Bent arrives at court before pleading guilty to possession of cocaine and affray.

Ashley Cole, with an air rifle, in Cobham.

To most, Ashley Cole is England's all-time greatest full-back but the three-time Premier League winner also made headlines for an infamous training ground air rifle incident.

Back in 2011 while playing for Chelsea, Ashley Cole accidentally shot and injured 21-year-old student Tom Cowan, who was on work experience at the Blues' training ground in Cobham, Surrey.

The Champions League winning left-back was reportedly 'larking about' with a .22 air rifle and accidentally shot Cowan from just five feet away.

The student had assumed he would get an invaluable experience on his brief visit to Cobham but instead had to be treated by medics and rest for the remainder of the day after the shot was fired.

Cole accidentally shot a 21-year-old on work experience at Chelsea's training ground.

Darren Bent, with a BB Gun, in Kesgrave.

Ex-England star Darren Bent ran into trouble early in his career when he was questioned over the alleged shooting of a 12-year-old boy with a ball-bearing gun.

While starring for his boyhood club Ipswich at the age of 20 in May 2004, Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause violence, before he was placed on bail and eventually released without charge pending further investigations.

According to a Suffolk Police statement at the time, a 12-year-old boy at a play area in Kesgrave had been struck in the back by a pellet from a ball-bearing gun (BB Gun). The incident was reported to authorities by his mother.

Bent, who was given a formal caution for his actions, went on to enjoy a fruitful career in the Premier League, representing the likes of Charlton, Tottenham, Sunderland and Aston Villa while also winning 13 caps for the Three Lions.

Early on his career Premier League legend Darren Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm.

Karim Adeyemi, with brass knuckles, in Germany.

The only member of this list to still be playing is Germany and Barcelona's Karim Adeyemi who was fined £396,000 in 2025 for possessing a pair of brass knuckles.

The former Borussia Dortmund forward was caught with the knuckles back in 2024, at the age of 22, but had to wait until the following year to receive his punishment.

Recent findings suggest that under German law the possession, procurement and use of brass knuckles is prohibited. The young winger avoided a public trial and a criminal record and was given a fine consisting of 60 daily payments of £6,600.

Although he never used the weapon, the German was in hot water  as he briefly lost his starting place in the German national team and at Borussia Dortmund.

The Westphalia giants released a statement saying: 'BVB always takes criminal allegations seriously and uses them as an opportunity to discuss them with its employees while respecting confidentiality obligations.'.

Adeyemi was lucky to dodge prison time after being charged with the possession of brass knuckles.

Diego Maradona, with an air rifle, in Buenos Aires.

Argentina icon Diego Maradona caused injuries to four people when he fired an air rifle at journalists and photographers while hiding behind a parked Mercedes outside his Buenos Aires home in February 1994.

Four years later, Maradona was found guilty of assault with a weapon and given a suspended prison sentence of two years and ten months, which was later reduced to an even two years.

To many he is the best of all time but Diego Maradona is hardly infallible off the pitch.

Despite appealing against the sentence which they claimed was 'too light', the journalists injured by Maradona said the verdict at least demonstrated there was 'justice for all' in Argentina.

'At least this exemplary case does show that there is justice for all,' mentioned Daniel Talamoni, one of the four reporters who sued the World Cup winner.

'When the case began four years ago, everyone said it was impossible. They would sentence a man idolised in Argentina and forgive everything.'.

Arda Turan, with an unlicensed gun, in a Turkish hospital.

Keen fans of European football will not need to be reminded of who Arda Turan is. But they may be surprised to learn that the former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona star has had some serious trouble with the law.

Turan somehow avoided a jail sentence after discharging an unlicensed firearm in a hospital.

In 2018 while on loan from Barcelona in his home country of Turkey at Istanbul Basaksehir, Turan got into an altercation with Turkish singer Berkay Sahin, who ended in hospital with a broken nose.

Then Turan turned up at the hospital that was treating Sahin with an unlicensed firearm, and fired a shot into the floor.

It has been revealed that he was eventually sentenced to two years and eight months behind bars for firing a gun to cause panic, illegal possession of weapons and intentional injury but the sentence was suspended for five years. Basaksehir also fined the midfielder £350,000 over the incident.

Nearly a decade after the incident, Turan now manages Ukrainian powerhouse Shakhtar Donetsk, joining the club in May of last year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

According to recent reports, if you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

Recent findings suggest that “With Alex, it is clear,” mentioned Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Industry observers note that quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

Recent findings suggest that what damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

Sources indicate that the next move declared the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

Industry observers note that it was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still revealed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Industry observers note that inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

Sources indicate that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The key thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

According to recent reports, “He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We revealed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the latest Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Industry observers note that andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola mentioned. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

Recent findings suggest that “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Sources indicate that ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

In a recent development, “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil noted. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

Youngsters will get their chance, Bruno Fernandes can thrive and touchline energy will be vital: Key lessons for Man United from incoming boss Mauricio Pochettino's 6-0 USA masterclass

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.
  • The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.

The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.

He will link up with United on Wednesday, but first must navigate the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie with Haiti on Tuesday.

Here, Pochettino cut a fairly reserved figure on the touchline as he was rewarded for trusting youth - and even saw his team score from a corner, something United don't do much of these days.

Without further ado, here are four things Manchester United fans learned from the win.

Mauricio Pochettino, dressed in a scarf, was fairly reserved as the United States beat Haiti 6-0.

Pochettino’s arrival spells good news for United’s proud tradition of promoting homegrown youth - it is glad tidings for the likes of Shea Lacey and Kobbie Mainoo. You wonder if, for a while, JJ Gabriel will look on forlornly from Real Madrid’s reserves.

The Argentinian handed out 13 debuts in the September-October international break, including to eight teenagers in one 4-1 victory over Peru.

Recent findings suggest that his strategy was no different here as he started 18-year-old Julian Hall up front and Diego Kochen, 20, in goal - both players he has given debuts to this year. He was rewarded, with Hall scoring his fourth goal in just five games for the United States, while Kochen kept a clean sheet.

Despite his affinity for the stars of tomorrow, he is a hard schoolmaster. In a column for The Athletic in 2022, he revealed that he sat a young Harry Kane down for a brutal meeting where he demonstrated him stats and clips to justify why he wasn’t playing him more.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino had known Kane’s potential from their first training session but wanted the ‘tough conversation’ to get the best out of him. Kane went on to score 169 goals under him for Tottenham, and now he’s the best player in the world.

His trust in fresh faces could inject some much-needed enthusiasm around the club, strengthen the squad's connection with the fanbase, and increase the energy levels in one of the Premier League's oldest, most lethargic teams.

The likes of Shea Lacey will be delighted at how Pochettino puts trust in younger players.

Julian Hall, 18, struck his fourth goal in five games for the United States under Pochettino.

Pochettino has a history of getting the most out of attacking midfielders such as Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, and Adam Lallana. You can add Cole Palmer to that list too, though he was primarily a right winger under him at Chelsea.

Manchester United desperately need him to get a tune out of Bruno Fernandes, who has cut a frustrated figure this season and whose creative efficiency has declined - though he still has nine goal involvements.

If Christian Pulisic’s performance against Haiti is anything to go by, Fernandes will be happy. The attacking midfielder scored twice, playing a free role and being given penalty duty.

The 28-year-old was also asked to muck in defensively, and that’s something Fernandes is willing to do. Across the seasons, he has often covered more ground than any of his team-mates.

Industry observers note that pochettino and Pulisic have seemingly had a distant relationship, despite the latter’s insistence to the contrary. The manager branded it ‘b*******’ when the AC Milan star opted out of the Gold Cup last year, and left him out of his selection a couple of months ago, bringing in 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan.

Asked about Pochettino's upcoming final game, Pulisic stated at full-time: 'We're treating it like any other game.' No emotion on display.

Depending on how you interpret Fernandes - either a die-for-the-badge club servant or a primadonna - Pochettino could draw the best or worst out of the Portuguese.

Pochettino often gets the best out of attacking midfielders - will he work well with Bruno Fernandes?

He has had a distant relationship with Christian Pulisic, but the AC Milan star scored twice here.

Pochettino tends to push his defensive lines high up the pitch and his strategy with the United States has been no different.

They were almost caught out for trying to play the offside trap early on as a simple ball from midfield sent Danley Jean Jacques through one-on-one, forcing Kochen into a good save.

Meanwhile, full-backs Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman were constantly pushing high and overlapping in his 4-2-3-1 system - although you’d obviously expect a strong level of intent when they’re favourites against Haiti.

Given his high-line tradition, Pochettino may well favour more mobile defenders such as Leny Yoro and Patrick Dorgu.

The battle for Harry Maguire will be to convince his new boss that his other qualities compensate for his lack of pace.

Pochettino takes inspiration from the frenetic football of Marcelo Bielsa, who managed him at Newell’s Old Boys in Argentina.

But he'll have to balance his philosophy with the reality of United's woeful defensive record this campaign. Just the 15 goals conceded in the last five games...

Pochettino revealed an eagerness to intervene early in the game - a possible boost after Michael Carrick suffered from slow starts.

Pochettino is typically seen as an animated character on the touchline, in contrast to Carrick's statesmanlike behaviour, but he spent lots of time in his seat here.

He has calmed down somewhat these days - though he did kick a crate of bottles in frustration at the World Cup - and didn’t even react much when his team scored.

Sources indicate that A major criticism of Carrick is that he takes too long to change things in-game, often going late with substitutions. Pochettino has traditionally leaned that way, too, but he was eager to influence proceedings here.

Even three minutes in, at a break while Antonee Robinson was being treated, he called Pulisic over for what looked like an intense tactical chat.

In a recent development, united have been plagued by slow starts this season, so it was encouraging to see Pochettino so alert and full of ideas early into the game. He could have coasted, really, but wanted to eke out every advantage.

  • Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.

Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta del Mezzogiorno, Il doppio ex, però, avverte che i giallorossi dovranno giocare tutte le proprie carte per cercare un risultato utile. Elogia inoltre l’avvio dei biancocelesti, pur indicando nell’Inter la sua favorita per lo scudetto.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, fascetti ha allenato il Lecce dalla stagione 1983/1984 alla 1985/1986. Con il presidente Franco Jurlano, il direttore sportivo Mimmo Cataldo e i calciatori della stagione 1984/1985 conquistò la prima promozione del club salentino in Serie A. Da giocatore aveva vestito anche la maglia della Lazio nel 1964/1965; dopo l’esperienza a Lecce, guidò i biancocelesti nel 1986/1987 e nel 1987/1988.

Recent findings suggest that A Roma ottenne prima la salvezza tra i cadetti, nonostante una penalizzazione iniziale di nove punti, poi la promozione in A. A 88 anni, dopo una vita trascorsa nel calcio tra campo e panchina, l’allenatore viareggino continua a seguire con attenzione la massima serie italiana e non solo.

Fascetti conserva un legame con entrambe le piazze: «Ho splendidi ricordi delle esperienze vissute in entrambe le piazze». Ripensando alla promozione leccese, aggiunge: «Due avventure che rammento con molto piacere. A Lecce, con un grande gruppo di lavoro, dalla dirigenza allo staff, dai calciatori ad ogni collaboratore, raggiungemmo un traguardo che tutti, nel Salento, sognavano. Fu una cavalcata straordinaria, come del resto i festeggiamenti di popolo che seguirono, coinvolgendo un intero territorio.».

Recent findings suggest that A quel traguardo Fascetti affianca il ricordo della morte di Michele Lorusso e Ciro Pezzella: «In giallorosso, purtroppo, ho vissuto anche un grave lutto, la tragica morte di Michele e di Ciro (le bandiere Lorusso e Pezzella ndr), che ancora oggi, a distanza di oltre 40 anni da quel maledetto 2 dicembre 1983, mi procura dolore solo a parlarne. Anche con la Lazio, però, ci siamo tolti delle belle soddisfazioni».

Recent findings suggest that nel giudizio di Fascetti, il percorso del Lecce rispecchia quello di una squadra chiamata a lottare fino alla fine per restare in Serie A: «Il Lecce sta effettuando il cammino che compete ad uno schieramento che ha l’obiettivo di lottare sino alla fine per cercare di meritare la permanenza». Sugli alti e bassi precisa: «Per le formazioni costruite per salvarsi, è scontato che vadano messi in conto degli alti e bassi. Non potrebbe essere diversamente. I giallorossi sono in linea con le aspettative e dovranno battagliare con i denti per provare a compiere l’ennesima impresa sportiva degli ultimi anni. La sofferenza fa parte del dna degli appassionati salentini».

Sources indicate that il presidente Saverio Sticchi Damiani e gli altri soci cercano di conciliare i risultati con un calcio sostenibile e conti in ordine. Finora, secondo Fascetti, ci sono riusciti. L’ex tecnico considera questa strada necessaria per i club di provincia: «Per le piccole realtà di provincia non ci sono alternative».

Il paragone di Fascetti va alla gestione che conobbe a Lecce: «Ai miei tempi, Jurlano e Cataldo si sono dimostrati bravissimi a regalare a più riprese la serie A al Lecce a costi limitati. Due autentici campioni. L’attuale proprietà si muove lungo la medesima direttrice ed è la scelta giusta, anche se i tifosi, in quanto tali, vorrebbero soffrire di meno».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

C'est une annonce pour le moins inattendue dans le monde du sport tricolore. Ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, Teddy Riner a officialisé sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 dans une vidéo publiée sur son compte X, tout en lançant son propre mouvement politique intitulé « La France qu'on veut ».

Le judoka français de 37 ans se lance ainsi en politique après avoir dominé le judo international. Quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde, Teddy Riner a bâti un palmarès exceptionnel qui le place au sommet de sa discipline. Alors que son avenir sportif restait au cœur des discussions depuis les Jeux de Paris, le Français surprend en ouvrant un tout autre chapitre personnel. Un virage spectaculaire.

It has been revealed that dans une vidéo publiée ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 sur son compte X, Teddy Riner a pris la parole face caméra afin de lever le voile sur ses intentions pour la prochaine présidentielle. Le judoka de 37 ans a officialisé sa démarche avec des mots simples et directs.

Industry observers note that conscient des réactions que son entrée en politique peut susciter, le quintuple champion olympique a tenu à devancer immédiatement les critiques concernant son manque d'expérience dans les fonctions publiques. Teddy Riner a ainsi déclaré : « Je sais ce qu'on va dire de moi. Il est fou, il n'est pas du sérail, il n'a pas les codes, il n'a jamais fait de politique. Mais posez-vous la question avec moi, qu'est-ce qui est fou aujourd'hui ? Je n'ai pas passé ma vie derrière un public, mais le combat a toujours fait partie de moi. » Une détermination affichée.

In a recent development, pour concrétiser ses ambitions, le judoka français de 37 ans a également fondé sa propre formation politique ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, baptisée « La France qu'on veut ». Cette prise de parole sur les réseaux sociaux a d'ailleurs été accompagnée d'un entretien accordé au quotidien Le Parisien pour préciser le sens de sa démarche. Dans cet échange, Teddy Riner revendique une volonté de rassemblement sans affiliation partisane, affirmant vouloir devenir un « président qui fédère » sans se situer à droite ou à gauche.

Industry observers note that en effet, le champion tricolore a expliqué que sa décision avait mûri dans le sillage direct de l'élan collectif suscité par les Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024. Porté par cette dynamique populaire, il entend désormais transposer cette ferveur sur le proposal politique. Ainsi, son mouvement politique refuse d'entrer dans les clivages traditionnels pour privilégier une adhésion commune à l'échelle du pays. Un projet ambitieux.

Sources indicate that toutefois, cette ambition politique ne pousse pas Teddy Riner vers la retraite sportive. Sur le plan des compétitions, sa dernière apparition individuelle remonte aux Jeux olympiques de Paris en août 2024, suivie d'une participation sous les couleurs du PSG Judo en Ligue des champions en décembre 2024. Malgré cette nouvelle démarche politique, le quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde de judo demeure bel et bien un athlète en activité.

Au-delà de l'élection présidentielle de 2027, Teddy Riner a ainsi fait part de son souhait de participer aux Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028 si ses futures responsabilités et les Français le lui permettent. Le judoka français lie donc son avenir sportif à la suite de son engagement public, avec en ligne de mire les Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Auteur de son premier but dans l'élite lors du match nul sur le terrain sarthois, Mamadou Coulibaly a suscité une vive polémique en mimant un geste d'égorgement. Le jeune milieu de l'AS Monaco se retrouve désormais sous la menace directe d'une lourde suspension.

According to recent reports, dimanche 8 novembre 2026, l'AS Monaco a été accrochée sur la pelouse du Mans FC (1-1) pour le compte de la 10e journée de Ligue 1. Si le club du Rocher espérait engranger des points précieux, la rencontre a été marquée par le geste de son joueur de 22 ans.

According to recent reports, titularisé dans l'entrejeu monégasque, Mamadou Coulibaly pensait passer une bonne soirée après avoir ouvert le score à la 40e minute de jeu. Mais la joie d'inscrire son tout premier but en Ligue 1 a rapidement viré au malaise lors de sa célébration. Le milieu monégasque s'est en effet dirigé vers le poteau de corner pour glisser sur les genoux, avant de tirer la langue et de mimer un geste d'égorgement avec son pouce sous la gorge. Un geste polémique.

Industry observers note that ce geste n'est malheureusement pas inédit en Principauté cette saison. En effet, cette célébration reproduit à l'identique celle effectuée par son partenaire de club Paris Brunner face à Strasbourg en septembre dernier, lors de la 4e journée de Ligue 1. Pour ce geste, le jeune attaquant avait été sanctionné par la commission de discipline de la LFP de quatre matches de suspension, dont deux fermes et deux avec sursis.

D'ailleurs, cette récidive au sein du même effectif met le joueur dans une situation extrêmement délicate. En raison de ce précédent disciplinaire très récent, Mamadou Coulibaly risque une sanction similaire d'au moins deux matches de suspension ferme devant la commission de discipline de la LFP. L'instance disciplinaire devrait se saisir rapidement du dossier pour trancher sur ce comportement. Un coup dur en perspective.

Conscient des remous provoqués par son geste, le joueur de 22 ans s'est exprimé devant les journalistes à l'issue de la rencontre. « Je tiens à m’excuser parce que j’ai cru comprendre que ça avait été mal compris. C’est un geste que j’ai fait par rapport un ami à moi qui m’a conseillé au sujet de la célébration. Je tiens à m'excuser si ça a pu heurter des gens. Maintenant, ce sont des choses qui se font dans d'autres championnats, je n'ai pas pensé que ça pourrait avoir des conséquences négatives », a ainsi déclaré Mamadou Coulibaly en zone mixte au micro des médias après Le Mans-Monaco.

In a recent development, toutefois, cette justification risque de ne pas suffire auprès de son entraîneur Filipe Luis. Le coach monégasque avait pourtant publiquement averti son groupe en septembre après l'affaire similaire, insistant sur l'exemplarité attendue : « Il a fait une erreur. Il l'a compris tout de suite. Il s'est excusé. Le club prend cette affaire très au sérieux (…). On espère que ça ne se reproduira plus », avait prévenu le technicien en conférence de presse. Au-delà de cette polémique extra-sportive, l'AS Monaco accueillera l'AJ Auxerre au stade Louis-II le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 20h45 pour la 11e journée de Ligue 1.

C'est la surprise majeure de ce rassemblement de novembre. Pour pallier le forfait sur blessure de Pierre Kalulu, le sélectionneur Zinédine Zidane a décidé d'appeler pour la première fois Saël Kumbedi en équipe de France ce lundi 9 novembre 2026. Une trajectoire fulgurante pour le latéral droit évoluant en deuxième division allemande.

According to recent reports, le premier jour du rassemblement à Clairefontaine a réservé un rebondissement de taille dans les rangs tricolores. En effet, Pierre Kalulu a dû déclarer forfait en raison d'une lésion aux ischios du membre inférieur gauche contractée ce week-end avec la Juventus. Face à ce coup dur dans le couloir droit, Zinédine Zidane s'est tourné vers Saël Kumbedi, alors que le joueur de 21 ans avait initialement été retenu par Gérald Baticle avec les Espoirs pour disputer deux rencontres amicales face à l'Italie à Brest et contre l'Angleterre à Bristol.

It has been revealed that comptant déjà neuf sélections avec les Bleuets, le défenseur franchit donc un cap décisif. Pour régler la pénurie à ce poste, le staff technique a délibérément privilégié la jeunesse du joueur de Wolfsburg plutôt que l'expérience de Jonathan Clauss, pourtant performant à Nice du haut de ses 34 ans et de ses quatorze sélections (2 buts). Un choix fort.

Sources indicate that avant d'atteindre le groupe de Zinédine Zidane, Saël Kumbedi a connu un parcours jalonné d'étapes intenses. Formé au Havre, le natif de Stains avait rejoint l'Olympique Lyonnais en 2022 contre un chèque d'un million d'euros, découvrant la Ligue 1 à seulement 17 ans sous la houlette de Peter Bosz avant d'enchaîner sous les ordres de Laurent Blanc. Au total, le défenseur a disputé 62 matches sous le maillot des Gones, dont quatre apparitions sur la scène européenne en Ligue Europa lors de l'exercice 2024-2025.

In a recent development, prêté au VfL Wolfsburg à l'été 2025, le latéral a ensuite été transféré définitivement le 1er janvier 2026 pour un montant de six millions d'euros. Toutefois, l'institution allemande, championne de Bundesliga en 2009 et installée dans l'élite sans discontinuer depuis 1997, a été reléguée en mai 2026 lors d'un barrage contre Paderborn (0-0, 2-1 a.p.). Un coup dur pour la formation allemande. Resté fidèle au club en 2. Bundesliga, Kumbedi est rapidement devenu un titulaire indiscutable sous les ordres de Tobias Strobl, malgré une blessure musculaire lui ayant fait manquer trois matches.

Cette convocation inattendue concrétise la passerelle directe établie entre la sélection A et les moins de 21 ans tricolores. Présent chez les Espoirs, le défenseur Nathan Zézé avait d'ailleurs rapporté le discours tenu par Zinédine Zidane :.

Le parcours de Saël Kumbedi en équipe de France démarre ainsi dans ce contexte de renouvellement. Les Bleus disputeront deux matches de Ligue des nations capitaux au cours de cette trêve internationale. Ils commenceront par un déplacement face à l'Italie à Milan, programmé le jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à 20h45. L'équipe de France recevra ensuite la Turquie à Bordeaux, le dimanche 15 novembre 2026 à 20h45.

'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.
  • Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

Sources indicate that erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport.

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

Recent findings suggest that 'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

Sources indicate that 'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

Recent findings suggest that 'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland stated.

'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

It has been revealed that the forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018.

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a upcoming nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that indicates everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I mentioned, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

It has been revealed that 'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'.

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was confirmed in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

In a recent development, le World 11 masculin 2026 a été configuré selon un schéma tactique très offensif, comprenant un gardien, trois défenseurs, trois milieux et quatre attaquants. Cette formation réunit plusieurs têtes d'affiche du football continental :.

Milieux : Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Rodri (FC Barcelone), Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain).

Attaquants : Erling Haaland (Manchester City), Kylian Mbappé (Real Madrid), Lionel Messi (Inter Miami), Lamine Yamal (FC Barcelone).

In a recent development, dans ce secteur offensif de gala, Kylian Mbappé s'impose comme l'unique footballeur français récompensé cette année. À ses côtés, Lionel Messi retrouve le World 11 masculin pour la première fois depuis 2023, enregistrant au passage sa 18e nomination. De son côté, le phénomène Lamine Yamal se paye le luxe d'établir un record en devenant le premier joueur à obtenir deux apparitions dans le onze de la FIFPRO avant ses 20 ans. Un record de précocité.

According to recent reports, au tableau des nations, l'Espagne s'affirme comme le pays le plus représenté dans ce onze avec quatre éléments plébiscités, à savoir David Raya, Pau Cubarsí, Rodri et Lamine Yamal. La sélection espagnole porte ainsi son total à 53 apparitions dans le FIFPRO World 11 masculin.

It has been revealed that À l'échelle des clubs, le Paris Saint-Germain et le FC Barcelone sont les clubs les plus représentés du scrutin masculin. Le club parisien compte en effet trois lauréats avec les deux défenseurs latéraux Achraf Hakimi et Nuno Mendes, ainsi que le milieu de terrain Vitinha. Le FC Barcelone installe de son côté Lamine Yamal, Rodri et Pau Cubarsí, qui bénéficient logiquement du sacre de l'Espagne lors de la Coupe du monde.

De son côté, le Real Madrid place deux joueurs majeurs dans cette formation idéale avec Jude Bellingham et Kylian Mbappé. L'institution madrilène comptait d'ailleurs au départ cinq nommés potentiels dans les listes globales : Thibaut Courtois, Marc Cucurella, Jude Bellingham et Kylian Mbappé chez les hommes, ainsi qu'Athenea del Castillo chez les femmes.

According to recent reports, cette distinction annuelle tire sa valeur de son mode de désignation, où les joueurs jugent directement leurs pairs sur l'ensemble de la planète. En effet, le scrutin masculin a réuni les votes de 19 806 footballeurs professionnels évoluant dans 73 pays différents. Une participation massive. Pour départager les nombreux prétendants et intégrer l'équipe type, la FIFPRO a appliqué une grille d'évaluation rigoureuse dès l'ouverture des votes.

Ainsi, la période de référence retenue pour analyser le rendement sur le terrain s'est étendue du 4 août 2025 au 19 juillet 2026 inclus. Au-delà des seules prestations sportives, une condition éliminatoire imposait aux nommés d'avoir disputé au minimum 30 matches officiels au cours de cet exercice.
