📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

In a recent development, "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

According to recent reports, only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Sources indicate that benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

In a recent development, united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

According to recent reports, “We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

Industry observers note that but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

Industry observers note that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

Sources indicate that it could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

It has been revealed that when Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes noted. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

Sources indicate that they did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

It has been revealed that as Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

In a recent development, it felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

Sources indicate that it’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

In a recent development, even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

It has been revealed that just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg.
  • According to recent reports, wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break.
  • Recent findings suggest that neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg. Freiburg – along with Niko Kovac’s Borussia Dortmund – have both taken advantage of record champions Bayern Munich dropping points against Cologne last night. Freiburg draw level with Bayern on points while Dortmund top the table after also narrowly edging out Borussia Mönchengladbach 0-1 away.

According to recent reports, wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break. Jan Gyamerah started at right back over Luca Sirch while Cole Campbell took the place of Germany U21 international Maurice Krattenmacher on the left wing. Schuster, meanwhile, employed just one change to the XI that began against Union Berlin 13 days ago. The star of that victory, Yuito Suzuki, was given a break after returning from international duty with Japan. German veteran Lucas Höler started in place of Suzuki in the No. 10 slot.

Recent findings suggest that neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes. In point of fact, willingness to intensely engage in direct duels remained high on both sides. Amid the many changes in possession, however, neither team was able to achieve much of a breakthrough. Freiburg did win a pair of corners and Igor Matanovic came close to earning a chance in the 9th minute. It would nevertheless be unfair to say that the Breisgauer guests looked the better squad. Possession remained split down the middle throughout the first quarter-of-an-hour.

Elversberg won their first corner in the 18th minute thanks to some hard work on the dribble from Leverkusen loanee Francis Onyeka. The hosts were able to swing the ball into the box several times after the set-piece, yet couldn’t produce an effort on target. Maximilian Rohr and Lukasz Poreba managed to dig out another Elversberg corner in the 23rd minute. David Mokwa forced a stellar save from Mio Backhaus off the corner, but the Saarland hosts again failed to get the ball headed goal-ward on the successive dead-ball.

Industry observers note that after the half-hour mark passed, the SVE began to look a tad more lively and creative. Gyamerah, Lukas Petkov, and Felix Keidel repeatedly got some solid attack charges going up the SVE right. The fact that the hosts gained an upper hand optically still produced little. Mokwa saw his attempt at a spectacular bicycle kick blocked in the 34th. Onyeka spurned a lovely play-in from Gyamerah in the 40th by losing the ball in the box. Apart from drawing a frustration-fueled yellow card out of Freiburg’s Jan-Niklas Beste, the promoted club had nothing to show for their efforts.

The match unquestionably maintained its intensity while undeniably featuring a steady loss of tempo.

According to recent reports, neither head coach opted to employ changes at the half. To the candid observer, these decisions were quite apparent. Schuster’s guests added a slight element of risk to their game, yet were still constrained by the fact that “paint the corner” passing around the box didn’t facilitate any danger. At the other end, Elversberg were gifted counter opportunities on both flanks in the opening ten minutes after the start, but noticeably lacked the pace to take true advantage of the accorded space. Onyeka came closest to creating a chance at the hour-mark, finding himself stymied centrally by a Maximilian Eggestein block.

The hosts eventually found themselves punished for failing to turn a slight optical advantage into a lead. Beste latched onto a long launch from SCF defender Philipp Lienhart in the 68th minute. After shielding the ball skillfully against SVE challenger Rohr, Beste actually inadvertently set up Igor Matanovic with a layoff. The Croat marksman nevertheless didn’t hesitate, reacting sharply to smack the ball deftly into the bottom right corner. Matanovic’s impressive ninth goal across all competitions this season gave the visiting Schwarzwälder a 1-0 lead.

With the deadlock finally broken, the encounter swiftly became more entertaining. A Keidel-led counter-attack shortly after the opening goal nearly led to an equalizer, but SVE captain Lukas Pinckert ultimately shot wide. Not long after being subbed on, Suzuki thought he had doubled Freiburg’s advantage in the 76th minute. The goal was chalked off due to a narrow offside decision.

Recent findings suggest that plenty of action ensued for a time until Schuster’s men settled into a more compact block and the Freiburg coach sent on some attacking reinforcements. As the clock ticked on towards full-time, Freiburg looked the more likely team to score. Fresh SCF attackers Vincenzo Grifo and Keisuke Goto opened up more space in the SCF attacking third. Eggestein and Philipp Treu saw late tries for the 2-0 blocked.

Nicolas Kristof (5) – Jan Gyamerah (7), Lukas Pinckert (6), Maximilian Rohr (4), Lasse Günther (5) – Felix Keidel (7), Łukasz Poręba (5) – Lukas Petkov (6), Francis Onyeka (4), Cole Campbell (5) – David Mokwa (4).

Substitutes: Luca Sirch (5), Noel Futkeu (5), Tom Zimmerschied (5), Maurice Krattenmacher (6), Raif Adam (-).

Mio Backhaus (6) – Philipp Treu (5), Matthias Ginter (6), Philipp Lienhart (7), Jordy Makengo (4) – Maximilian Eggestein (4), Yannik Engelhardt (4) – Niklas Beste (6), Lucas Höler (3), Derry Scherhant (6) – Igor Matanovic (6).

Substitutes: Cyriaque Irié (5), Yuito Suzuki (6), Vincenzo Grifo (6), Keisuke Goto (6).

In a recent development, the Austrian central defender earns our distinction primarily for his decisive contribution to Freiburg’s winning goal. Lienhart’s expertly measured long ball in the 68th minute enabled Niklas Beste to break forward and ultimately set up Igor Matanovic’s finish. In a match largely characterized by midfield stalemates and limited attacking opportunities, Lienhart’s vision made the difference. The 30-year-old registered 74 touches, completed 83 percent of his 52 attempted passes, and covered 10.1 kilometres over the full 90 minutes. His impressive top speed of 32.2 km/h also deserves mention.

Sources indicate that freiburg striker Igor Matanovic is convinced that teammate Niklas Beste deliberately set up his match-winning goal against Elversberg on Saturday afternoon. Speaking to Get German Football News in the mixed zone following Freiburg’s narrow 1-0 away victory, the Croatian international rejected the suggestion that Beste’s decisive touch had been accidental.

Recent findings suggest that the 68th-minute goal finally broke the deadlock in an intensely contested encounter at the Kaiserlinde. Austrian defender Philipp Lienhart initiated the move with a long ball towards Beste, who managed to shield possession against Elversberg’s Maximilian Rohr.

Industry observers note that beste’s subsequent layoff appeared somewhat fortuitous, but Matanovic reacted immediately to steer the ball into the bottom right corner. The striker’s ninth goal across all competitions this season ultimately proved sufficient to secure all three points for Julian Schuster’s side.

The 23-year-old believes that his understanding with Beste, rather than simple good fortune, made the decisive difference. Matanovic pointed to the familiarity between Freiburg’s attacking players, emphasizing that the entire team has developed an instinctive awareness of one another’s movements.

The striker also recalled his earlier observations about the special chemistry within Schuster’s squad. That collective understanding has helped Freiburg negotiate difficult Bundesliga encounters, including Saturday’s hard-fought victory over a spirited Elversberg side.

The latest success follows Freiburg’s 2-0 home victory against Union Berlin before the international break and further strengthens the Breisgau club’s position near the top of the Bundesliga table.

In a recent development, the south Baden side responded to a 1-3 home defeat against Bayern on matchday seven by defeating Wolfsburg in the Pokal. They’ve not lost since, capturing five consecutive victories on the spin.

According to recent reports, “I know that Niki likes making that run,” Matanovic told Get German Football News in the mixed zone. “And the way he laid the ball off, I think a lot of people will say it was accidental. I think he wanted it exactly that way. I’m convinced of that.”.

“I already told you at the beginning of the season that this team is really special,” the striker continued. “I had the feeling that we had an instinctive understanding. Actually, it’s not just a feeling. We really do have that understanding.”.

“Everyone knows which runs the other players make, and Niki knows that I’ll naturally follow his run,” Matanovic explained. “He laid the ball off perfectly for me, allowing me to put it away nicely.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, freiburg striker Igor Matanovic believes his team’s newfound ability to grind out difficult victories represents a significant step forward under head coach Julian Schuster. Speaking to Get German Football News in the mixed zone after Saturday’s 1-0 Bundesliga victory over Elversberg, the Croatian international explained why Freiburg are now consistently collecting points in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Matanovic’s 68th-minute winner against the promoted Saarland club extended Freiburg’s winning streak to five matches across all competitions. The Breisgauer have recovered impressively from their October struggles, defeating Wolfsburg in the DFB-Pokal before adding victories against Augsburg, Trabzonspor, Union Berlin, and Elversberg.

The latest success also moved Freiburg level on points with Bayern Munich near the top of the Bundesliga table.

In a recent development, the 23-year-old believes Freiburg’s improvement reflects considerably more than a fortunate run of results. Matanovic emphasized the squad’s collective resilience, suggesting that the team’s current momentum has been built upon a healthy foundation and a willingness to discuss shortcomings openly.

The striker specifically recalled Freiburg’s response to three consecutive defeats earlier in the campaign, praising his teammates for refusing to allow the setbacks to undermine their confidence.

Saturday’s hard-fought victory provided another illustration of that mentality. As documented in GGFN‘s match report and player ratings, Freiburg struggled to create clear opportunities against a spirited Elversberg side before finally breaking through in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that matanovic explained that maintaining concentration and relying on familiar tactical principles were particularly important in such circumstances. Aggressive pressing, collective defensive work, and persistence in winning possession eventually helped Freiburg create the decisive opening.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s tremendous. Obviously, it’s very nice to be collecting the points as well,” Matanovic mentioned when asked about Freiburg’s five consecutive victories. “I think that’s the difference compared to last season. What we were missing were the points. We often played well, but then we’d come away with just one point. Now we’re winning the dirty games.”.

“Even recently against Union Berlin, you know how unpleasant they can be to play against, and we still managed to win 2-0,” the Croatian continued. “There’s genuinely a very high level of quality in this team, and of course we’re enjoying a certain flow. But the flow we have comes from this healthy foundation that we can always rely upon. I often mention the three consecutive defeats we suffered. How many teams collapse after something like that? How many lose their confidence?”.

Industry observers note that “But we always get back to basics,” Matanovic went on. “We address things openly and honestly, and that’s how we find our way back into our flow. Right now, we’re simply very, very difficult opponents to face. You have to maintain your focus, especially when you’re not creating many chances or opportunities. Then you have these basics you can rely upon. Keep pushing forward, press high, make life difficult for the opposition, and block plenty of balls.”.

“I think we also won possession back many times in the first half,” Matanovic concluded. “That’s something we force through our own efforts, and that’s how we eventually create scoring chances again. There weren’t many chances, but I think we could even have rewarded ourselves with more goals in the end.”.

Nmecha’s most recent goal celebration till exhibited religious overtones, though the Dortmund professional did not repeat the crowning gesture that sparked the controversy in the first place. Nmecha spoke on the matter afterwards.

The controversy began following Dortmund’s 2-1 victory over SV Elversberg before the international break. Nmecha celebrated both goals by symbolically removing a crown and placing it on the ground. The gesture is associated with the evangelical football network Ballers in God, whose activities and reported positions on homosexuality and other social issues have attracted criticism.

Recent findings suggest that get German Football News previously reported on Dortmund’s response to the controversy, including objections raised by the club’s Fan and Supporters Department. Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke subsequently appealed to Nmecha to reconsider the gesture, emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary divisions among supporters.

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp later indicated that the matter had been resolved following a personal conversation with Nmecha. Klopp explained that the midfielder had agreed not to repeat the celebration in its controversial form. Nmecha indeed opted for a different celebration after scoring against Gladbach, sliding towards the corner flag before kneeling and crossing his arms over his chest. After the full-time whistle, Nmecha dropped to his knees and engaged in prayer.

Sources indicate that dortmund sporting director Ole Book defended Nmecha’s right to express his Christian faith, distinguishing Saturday’s celebration from the gesture that had provoked criticism. Meanwhile, Ballers in God subsequently shared images of Nmecha’s latest celebration on social media, interpreting three of his gestures as symbolizing a direct communication of the player’s Christian faith.

It has been revealed that “What people were saying didn’t ring true to me,” Nmecha told Sky Germany. “That celebration was simply about my faith, laying the crown on the ground for Jesus and giving him the glory. That doesn’t mean I’ll never do that celebration again.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that the glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning.
  • For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline said. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

It has been revealed that for England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

Sources indicate that this was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

Sources indicate that this felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain.

In a recent development, once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

For the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

Industry observers note that this year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Sources indicate that many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain.

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it.

Sources indicate that and then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted company of the other players on two fine teams.

Bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

Bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

According to recent reports, he has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be remarked about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

Harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

Industry observers note that the man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or.

With them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he showed when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

It has been revealed that he and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

Now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that eintracht Frankfurt supporters provided one of the most heartwarming moments of Saturday’s Bundesliga action after a technical malfunction silenced the sound system at Deutsche Bank Park. Rather than allow the disruption to spoil the occasion, the Frankfurt faithful took matters into their own hands, providing their own musical accompaniment ahead of the Eagles’ 1-0 home victory over TSG Hoffenheim.

The extraordinary scenes began before kickoff when the Bundesliga club confirmed that its stadium-wide sound system had suffered a technical failure. A message displayed on the stadium’s video screens warned supporters that the usual announcements and musical accompaniment would be unavailable until further notice. An unusually quiet atmosphere accompanied the players’ warm-ups. Frankfurt’s famously passionate supporters nevertheless had other ideas.

At the request of the stadium announcer, who could still be heard faintly, supporters in Frankfurt’s Nordwestkurve began singing the club’s traditional anthem, Im Herzen von Europa, without any musical accompaniment. The spontaneous performance proved particularly fitting given the song’s history. The beloved Eintracht anthem was originally recorded by Frankfurt’s police choir, whose rendition has become an integral part of the club’s home matchday tradition.

On Saturday, however, the supporters themselves assumed responsibility for the performance.

The club couldn’t resist making light of the unusual circumstances.

Industry observers note that “‘Im Herzen von Europa’, today performed not by the police choir, but by the stadium choir. That’s a first,” Eintracht observed in its matchday coverage. Nor did the impromptu entertainment stop with the anthem. Supporters also enthusiastically took over the team announcements, shouting out the starting lineup and providing a suitably rousing welcome as both teams emerged onto the pitch.

It has been revealed that the technical difficulties had threatened to deprive the afternoon of its familiar atmosphere. Instead, they had given the Frankfurt faithful an opportunity to demonstrate precisely why the Waldstadion remains one of German football’s most atmospheric venues.

The singing continued into the opening stages of the match, with the Nordwestkurve providing vocal encouragement as Adi Hütter’s side sought to make the most of their home advantage. Frankfurt’s supporters were rewarded in the 25th minute when Jonathan Burkardt finished an excellent attacking move to give the hosts the lead.

According to recent reports, although faint goal music and an announcement could reportedly be heard amid the technical difficulties, the home fans hardly needed any encouragement to celebrate. There was further excitement before halftime when goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved Andrej Kramaric’s penalty in the 41st minute. Frankfurt then received a spot kick of their own, only for Hoffenheim goalkeeper Oliver Baumann to deny Burkardt three minutes later.

It has been revealed that the stadium’s sound system was finally restored for the second half, but the supporters had already ensured that the unusual afternoon would be remembered for something considerably more enjoyable than a technical malfunction. Frankfurt ultimately protected their narrow lead to claim all three points, securing a third consecutive Bundesliga home victory.

According to recent reports, eintracht CEO Axel Hellmann was rather less enthusiastic about the technical difficulties. Speaking after the match, the club executive used the incident to renew his calls for a upcoming stadium, pointing to increasingly frequent problems with the ageing arena’s electricity, lighting, and other infrastructure. Hellmann maintained that the situation would only deteriorate in the coming years and reiterated the need for a replacement venue, ideally completed by 2038.

One can certainly appreciate Hellmann’s concerns. Nevertheless, there is a certain irony in the fact that the stadium’s shortcomings should become so apparent on an afternoon when its supporters demonstrated precisely what makes the place so special.

Recent findings suggest that as Get German Football News noted in a feature on Germany’s most beloved traditional stadiums last November, the Waldstadion occupies a particularly cherished place in the hearts of the German footballing public. Nestled in the forest south of Frankfurt’s bustling financial district, the historic ground retains an identity that no corporate naming-rights agreement has ever managed to displace.

Whatever the future holds for the Waldstadion, Saturday’s events offered another reminder that the most crucial component of Frankfurt’s famous home atmosphere requires neither electricity nor expensive technology.

Just a few thousand willing voices.

Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Malik Tillman has admitted that recent criticism from the club’s supporters has diminished his appreciation of their applause. Speaking after Saturday’s 4-0 Bundesliga victory over SC Paderborn, the 24-year-old former Germany U21 and current USMNT international offered a remarkably candid assessment of his relationship with the Leverkusen faithful despite producing his best performance of the season.

In a recent development, tillman assisted Afonso Moreira’s opening goal with an excellent pass and impressed with several further attacking contributions. When head coach Carles Martínez substituted the midfielder in the 67th minute, the BayArena crowd responded with enthusiastic applause and chants of his name.

The reception contrasted sharply with Leverkusen’s recent 4-2 home defeat against VfB Stuttgart, when Tillman was greeted by boos upon entering the pitch as a substitute. Rather than welcome the change in attitude, however, the former Bayern Munich academy player suggested that such reactions no longer carried much significance for him.

Sources indicate that get German Football News previously reported on Tillman’s frustrations with Leverkusen supporters following a revealing interview with the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger in August. The American acknowledged that criticism of his performances was sometimes justified, but emphasized that some reactions had become excessively personal. Tillman also discussed difficulties with former coach Kasper Hjulmand and expressed disappointment over the support he had received from the club’s management.

Recent findings suggest that the midfielder arrived from PSV Eindhoven in the summer of 2025 for approximately €35 million. The considerable expectations accompanying his arrival have frequently proven difficult to fulfill. Our detailed preseason assessment of Leverkusen highlighted Tillman’s difficulties establishing himself in Martínez’s plans amid increased competition for attacking positions.

Saturday’s performance nevertheless offered fresh encouragement. Tillman demonstrated the technical quality and creativity that persuaded Leverkusen to invest heavily in his services. Whether the latest display will help repair his relationship with sections of the club’s support remains another matter.

“I have confidence in myself, but playing a good game naturally strengthens that confidence even further,” Tillman explained after Saturday’s match, as reported by Kicker. “I have to keep going here, no matter what happens. But I’m happy with my performance.”.

Asked how he felt about receiving applause after previously being booed, the American offered a notably different response.

“It’s difficult to say at this point,” Tillman admitted. “I don’t really care anymore. I don’t know. Of course, it sucks when you get booed, and at the end of the day, it doesn’t really mean much to me anymore when people cheer or shout my name.”.

L’esterno ha iniziato la stagione in modo convincente. Per Bech, se manterrà questo rendimento, potrà disputare la migliore annata della sua carriera. Il giornalista indica finora come suo riferimento la stagione 2022/23, chiusa da capocannoniere della Superliga danese. In quell’annata Isaksen segnò anche due gol contro la Lazio: Bech ritiene probabile che il club biancoceleste abbia cominciato allora a interessarsi a lui.

Sul contratto, Bech ritiene che il giocatore sarebbe disponibile a prolungare l’accordo con la Lazio, ma lascia aperte le possibilità: alla scadenza mancano meno di due anni. A suo giudizio Isaksen sembra felice a Roma e a proprio agio in Italia, come il calciatore stesso ha dichiarato in più occasioni.

  • Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s newly introduced manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s newly introduced manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February and has taken a significant pay cut to take over at Palace, who languish at the bottom of the Premier League.

However, he will earn more than his predecessor, Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after winning just two of his ten league matches in charge.

Newly introduced Palace boss Frank mentioned: ‘It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

‘Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.’.

Across his spells at Brentford and Tottenham, Frank has managed 178 Premier League matches with a 34 per cent win rate.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Bernardo Cueva, who worked with Frank at Brentford before being poached to become the Blues' set-piece specialist.

We are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager 🤝ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S pic.twitter.com/zv2vMPGPFz.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Cueva (right), who worked with Frank at Brentford.

According to recent reports, but Cueva may now be elevated back to the forefront of football if Palace can strike an agreement to bring him in to join Frank’s backroom staff. It is said Chelsea paid Brentford around £1million in compensation to hire him in 2024 at a time when his stock was high.

Sources indicate that cueva arrived at Chelsea in 2024. However, Daily Mail Sport revealed in the last summer how the 39-year-old Mexican’s role was changing after two seasons of work as Xabi Alonso’s side hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa as their new lead on set-plays.

Cueva has not been seen since then, either in training at Cobham or at matches at Stamford Bridge, but continued to work for Chelsea in more of an analytical role behind the scenes.

Club sources stressed at the time that it should not be seen as a demotion, and he is still listed on the first-team staff section of the website under the title ‘technical analyst’.

Chelsea are due to play Palace in two weeks' time at the Bridge on Wednesday, December 2.

Chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive acquisition in 2024.

Before joining Brentford in 2020 and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his fresh kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this upcoming Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Sources indicate that jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo.

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very vital to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”.

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

According to recent reports, their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Industry observers note that vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Recent findings suggest that buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1.

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn.

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

According to recent reports, mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle glitch so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Sources indicate that addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He stated: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

Recent findings suggest that “We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [significant] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

It has been revealed that “We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”.

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH.

According to recent reports, emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of significant-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s newly introduced-look crew.

Sources indicate that morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his latest recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.
